fields.description:
## Context
MCP transition_ticket and claim_ticket do not expose write parameters already supported by the library and CLI. Live FastMCP schemas omit transition reason, caused_by, ref, and force, and omit claim force. Undeclared payload keys are discarded before the registered callable runs. This makes compliant reason-required closes, explicit culprit attribution, explicit completion refs, and authorized plan-gate bypass unreachable over MCP.

The signed 2026-08-18 operator ruling on restoring-shallow-blobfish rescinds the older CLI/library-only force policy: force is allowed through every surface, while the absent certified attestation remains the audit signal. Deprecated force_close stays excluded.

## Proven root cause
The handwritten MCP callable signatures in src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py were not kept in parity with the library surface. FastMCP 1.29 derives its JSON schema and argument model from those signatures, so it drops undeclared extras. Independently, the handwritten adapter calls forward only close_class for transition and assignee for claim, so adding schema fields alone would still lose them. Later caused_by and ref capabilities also stopped at this adapter boundary.

A four-case runtime probe confirmed the mechanism: live schemas omitted every reported field; capture stubs saw only close_class or assignee; an equivalent FastMCP tool with declared fields received exact sentinels; MCP ref selected HEAD instead of the requested older commit; and MCP caused_by closed without the edge while the library produced it.

## Repair plan
- Add library-compatible parameters to the registered MCP signatures: transition force bool, reason string, caused_by string, ref optional string; claim force optional reason-bearing string.
- Forward every parameter unchanged to rebar.transition or rebar.claim.
- Replace the rescinded no-force tool prose with the absent-attestation audit model and keep force_close explicitly unavailable.
- Replace the stale negative surface contract with positive schema assertions.
- Add lifecycle tests through the real registered FastMCP tools for reason-required close, caused_by, explicit ref, and both start-work force paths.
- Keep all other transition and claim semantics in the shared library/core; add no dependency or new bypass implementation.

## Test contract card
- Trigger: call the real registered MCP tools with each newly exposed parameter.
- Boundary: FastMCP schema and validation -> MCP adapter -> public library facade -> existing command core.
- Postconditions: declared fields appear in input schemas; exact values reach the shared core; reason-required close persists close_reason; caused_by writes the edge; explicit ref reaches verification/signing at that commit; transition force and claim force preserve their distinct library types and bypass semantics.
- Negative controls: absent or false/empty force preserves gating; reason-required close without reason remains rejected; deprecated force_close remains absent.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] transition_ticket exposes caused_by, ref, and reason-bearing optional force.
- [x] claim_ticket exposes reason-bearing optional force.
- [x] Every added parameter delegates unchanged to the existing library core.
- [x] MCP caused_by produces the same culprit edge as the library.
- [x] MCP ref targets and signs the requested immutable commit rather than HEAD.
- [x] MCP transition force covers both start-work and completion-close bypasses with shared audit semantics.
- [x] Absent force and a missing required close reason remain rejected as before.
- [x] force_close and a distinct close-reason field remain unavailable over MCP.
- [x] MCP tool prose describes absent certification as the audit signal.
- [x] Focused tests pass.
- [x] make lint passes.
- [x] make typecheck passes.
